entities.name: Abd al-Muttalib
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abd al-Muttalib was the fourth chief of the Quraysh tribal confederation and grandfather of the Islamic prophet Muhammad.

Born in Mecca, Arabia, around 570 CE, Abd al-Muttalib played a crucial role in shaping the early Islamic community.

Abd al-Muttalib's leadership and diplomatic efforts helped secure a peace treaty with the neighboring tribes, allowing the Quraysh to maintain control over the sacred city of Mecca.

His legacy extended beyond his own tribe, influencing the development of Islam and the expansion of the Arabian Peninsula.

One of the most striking aspects of Abd al-Muttalib's life was his connection to the Kaaba, the holiest site in Islam, where he oversaw the restoration of the Black Stone, a sacred relic believed to have been brought to Earth by the angel Gabriel.
